answer: In an agent economy, each participant must stake resources to light a lantern that illuminates their identity graph. A trellis of interlocking reputation links forms over time, where new agents can only enter through a verified inlet controlled by existing high-stake nodes. Creating thousands of sybil identities requires funding and maintaining separate lanterns plus building authentic trellis connections, imposing linear capital and time costs that scale with attack size and make mass forgery uneconomical.
